scenario_name: Positive partial cap on the Normal tranche
exposes: Normal nominal 1.0 capped to a positive partial amount by insufficient funding; the later escalation tranche's nominal size remains 1.0 (not resized), independently capped by ordinary funding rules (SD-4)

parameters.execution_valuation_rule_note: Declared FIXTURE PARAMETER, not a Baseline execution-price determination. P1-1/OD-04 untouched. Satisfies OD-03.

hand_derived_expectations.note: Hand-reasoned: annual budget is only 0.5 units for the year. 01-05 NORMAL fires nominal 1.0, but only 0.5 is available -> accepted=0.5 (capped=true), capacity consumed=0.5 (actual accepted amount, per the SD-4/SD-5 consistency check — not the nominal 1.0). 01-07 LARGE_DROP: the prior Normal acceptance was positive (0.5 > 0) so the escalation gate IS satisfied and the tranche fires; its nominal size remains 1.0 (not resized to 0.5, and not the remaining capacity of 1.5) — this is exactly what proves the nominal size is independent of the first tranche's capped outcome. It is then independently capped against funding: available is now exactly 0 (0.5-0.5), so accepted=0. This is a zero-unit OUTCOME of ordinary funding capping on an eligible, fired tranche — distinct from D5, where the tranche itself never becomes eligible to fire.
